full_judgment: 7. The High Court Division primarily, because of the memo dated March 31, 1985 i.e. the Memo whereby it was communicated to the Assistant Commissioner Settlement, that, the property is not an abandoned property held that, once the property which was found not abandoned property, the subsequent gazette notification treating the property as abandoned property cannot be considered legal. The High Court Division further of the view that, there was no reliable material before the Court of Settlement to consider Wali Alam and Monzorr Alam left the country during the war of liberation and that, their whereabouts were not known. The High Court Division also observed that, in the background of the facts and circumstances of the case "the normal presumption that, Wali Alam and Monzoor Alam were present in Bangladesh at the relevant time and period, when P.0.16 of 1972 came into operation on 28.02.1972 and they being in possession of the house sold the same to Mrs. Mahafuza Hyder Chowdhury vide 2 Kabalas dated 25.06.1974 and thereafter, Mrs. Mahafuza Hydcr Chowdhury, while in possession sold the same to writ ,petitioner vide Kabala dated 18.09.76, who got mutated the house in his name vide Annexure-C dated 21.01.1986, when the Government vide Annexure-B dated 31.03.1985 admitted that, the house in question was not an abandoned property and, when in view of Annexure-C, the Government mutated the name of petitioner for the house in office record and, when the writ petitioner has been in peaceful possession of the house on payment of rents vide Annexure-E (1) and E(2), there is no scope to treat the house as Abandoned Property.
